summary: On 18 Syawwal 1447 Ustaz Azlan continues with episode 37 on the jinn embracing Islam and the Prophet SAW receiving protection from non-Muslims. After explaining the class schedule and balancing knowledge with action, he tells of the journey home from Ta'if: Addas accepts Islam, the Prophet SAW stops at Nakhlah, and a group of jinn hear his recitation and return to preach to their people (Al-Ahqaf 29-32, Surah Al-Jinn, the hadiths of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud). The ustaz sets out basic principles about the jinn and our limits regarding that world. Then the Prophet SAW, unable to enter Makkah, sends envoys to Al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq and Suhail ibn Amr, who refuse, and Mut'im ibn Adi gives protection and escorts him in. The class closes on not despairing, wonder at the Quran, pragmatic cooperation and harmony in a plural society.
keyPoints: On the way home from Ta'if the Prophet SAW stopped at Nakhlah and a group of jinn heard his recitation without his knowing.
The jinn went straight back to preach to their people, and Allah recorded their dialogue in Al-Ahqaf 29-32 and Surah Al-Jinn.
Jinn include the righteous, believers who sin, those seeking truth, and devils; we are not charged with preaching to jinn nor allowed to deal with them.
Unable to enter Makkah, the Prophet SAW trusted that Allah would open a way but still planned strategically.
Al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq and Suhail ibn Amr declined to give protection, but Mut'im ibn Adi accepted and escorted the Prophet SAW with his sons.
The Prophet SAW did not forget Mut'im's favour though he was not Muslim, and mentioned him after Badr.
Lessons: do not despair in da'wah, feel wonder at the Quran, and cooperate pragmatically while holding to tawhid.

lessons.title: Space out lessons
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW scheduled reminders so the companions would not tire.

lessons.title: Balance knowledge and action
lessons.body: Neither only entertainment nor only lectures at the expense of duties.

lessons.title: Cherish the gift of guidance
lessons.body: Many know the Prophet SAW but do not follow him.

lessons.title: Da'wah reaches unexpected places
lessons.body: The jinn crossed paths with him at exactly the right moment; we do not know who benefits.

lessons.title: Listen to the Quran in silence
lessons.body: The Quran is not background noise while we chat.

lessons.title: Feel wonder at the Quran
lessons.body: The jinn called it amazing; we should ask how much we feel that.

lessons.title: Jinn also have a choice
lessons.body: Jinn have intellect and can choose good or bad like humans.

lessons.title: Do not over-focus on the jinn world
lessons.body: We are not charged with dealing with it; leave ruqyah matters to experts.

lessons.title: Trust and effort
lessons.body: Trust that Allah opens a way, and also act.

lessons.title: Think strategically in da'wah
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW weighed who could be approached to open a way.

lessons.title: Do not forget favours from non-Muslims
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW remembered Mut'im though he died not Muslim.

lessons.title: Live in harmony in a plural society
lessons.body: Both sides must keep sensitivity and nurture friendships from childhood.

lessons.title: Do not despair in da'wah
lessons.body: Surah Al-Jinn follows the story of Nuh to steady hearts.

lessons.title: Allah shows the impact of good
lessons.body: Even if we do not see results, Allah may show them.

lessons.title: Cooperate without relaxing tawhid
lessons.body: We work together on shared matters and never tone down tawhid.

dalil.context: Allah sent a group of jinn to the Prophet SAW to hear the Quran; they told each other to be silent and listen.
dalil.translation: We sent a group of jinn to you [Prophet] to listen to the Quran. When they heard it, they said to one another, ‘Be quiet!’ Then when it was finished they turned to their community and gave them warning.

dalil.context: The jinn said they heard a book revealed after Musa.
dalil.translation: They said, ‘Our people, we have been listening to a Scripture that came after Moses, confirming previous scriptures, giving guidance to the truth and the straight path.

dalil.context: The jinn's call to their people to answer the Messenger.
dalil.translation: Our people, respond to the one who calls you to God. Believe in Him: He will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful torment.’

dalil.context: A warning that whoever does not answer cannot escape punishment.
dalil.translation: Those who fail to respond to God’s call cannot escape God’s power anywhere on earth, nor will they have any protector against Him: such people have clearly gone far astray.

dalil.context: Surah Al-Jinn opens with the revelation that jinn listened and called the Quran amazing.
dalil.translation: Say [Prophet], ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn once listened in and said, “We have heard a wondrous Quran,

dalil.context: The jinn believed and vowed not to associate others with Allah.
dalil.translation: that gives guidance to the right path, and we have come to believe it––We shall never set up partners with our Lord––

dalil.context: Exalted is our Lord's majesty above taking a wife or child.
dalil.translation: and that He––exalted be the glory of our Lord!––has neither spouse nor child.

dalil.context: Criticism of the foolish leader who said outrageous things about Allah.
dalil.translation: Outrageous things have been said about God by the foolish among us,

dalil.context: We thought neither man nor jinn would lie about Allah.
dalil.translation: although we had thought that no man or jinn would [dare to] tell a lie about Him.

dalil.context: Some people sought refuge with leaders of the jinn, making them more arrogant.
dalil.translation: Men have sought refuge with the jinn in the past, but they only misguided them further.

dalil.context: Humans thought Allah would not send any messenger.
dalil.translation: They thought, as you did, that God would never raise anyone from the dead.

dalil.context: The jinn found the heavens filled with guards and flaming meteors.
dalil.translation: We tried to reach heaven, but discovered it to be full of stern guards and shooting stars––

dalil.context: Among the jinn are the righteous and others less so.
dalil.translation: Some of us are righteous and others less so: we follow different paths.

dalil.context: Jinn were created from smokeless fire.
dalil.translation: the jinn out of smokeless fire.

dalil.context: The ustaz reads it in detail as the backdrop.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW went with companions to the market of Ukaz; devils were barred from heavenly news and pelted with fire, so they spread out to find why. A group heading to Tihamah met the Prophet SAW at Nakhlah leading Fajr, heard the Quran and said: this is what stopped us.

dalil.context: Unlike the Bukhari hadith, it tells how he went to teach them.
dalil.translation: The companions lost the Prophet SAW one night and searched; at dawn he came from Hira and said a caller from the jinn had come and he recited the Quran to them. They were shown traces of the jinn's gathering, and he forbade cleaning oneself with bones and dung as they are food of their brothers among the jinn.

dalil.context: The ustaz uses it to explain a class schedule that is not daily.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW chose particular days to give reminders for fear that the companions would grow bored.

dalil.context: Shows the Prophet SAW took human feelings into account.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW noticed bored faces and asked; they said they missed returning to their families, so he postponed the class.

dalil.context: His answer when Zayd asked how to re-enter Makkah.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW told Zayd that Allah would make a way out of what they saw.

dalil.context: Said to be a Bukhari hadith; he recalled Mut'im's favour though he was not Muslim.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said that if Mut'im ibn Adi were alive and spoke about the captives, he would free them for his sake.
